## Gender in the noun phrase {.smaller}

|        | Singular | Plural |
|--------|----------|--------|
| German | **der** Stuhl, **die** Tür, **das** Buch | **die** Stühle, **die** Türen, **die** Bücher |
| Dutch  | **de** stoel, **het** boek | **de** stoelen, **de** boeken |

- **Gender** is a lexical property of the noun: *car* is **das** Auto, **la** voiture, **el** coche, **de** auto.
- **Number** is set by the context: one chair or two.

::: {.claim}
In both languages the article marks gender in the singular only.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 170 to 172
:::

## The task: picture-word interference

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.stim}
::: {.pic}
🪑
:::
::: {.word}
KLEID
:::
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
- **Say:** *der Stuhl* 'the chair'
- **Ignore:** *Kleid* 'dress', neuter (*das*)
- **Congruent distractor:** *Keks* 'cookie', masculine (*der*)
- **Measure:** time to speech onset
:::
::::

::: {.claim}
Gender congruency effect: naming is slower when the distractor's gender differs from the picture name's.
:::

::: footer
Items from Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Appendix A; effect first reported by Schriefers 1993
:::

## Where the effect shows up, and where it does not

- **Found:** Dutch (Schriefers 1993; Van Berkum 1997; La Heij et al. 1998), German (Schriefers & Teruel 2000).
- **Absent with bare nouns:** naming the picture without an article (La Heij et al. 1998).
- **Not found:** Italian, Catalan, Spanish, French (Miozzo & Caramazza 1999; Costa et al. 1999; Alario & Caramazza 2002).

::: {.prompt}
Why would Dutch and German show the effect when Romance languages do not?
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 170 to 171
:::

## Early and late article choice

- **Italian:** the article depends on gender **and** the sound of the next word.
  - *il tavolo* 'the table', *lo strano tavolo* 'the strange table'
  - *lo scienziato* 'the scientist', *il grande scienziato* 'the great scientist'
- **German, Dutch:** gender, number, and case alone fix the article.

::: {.claim}
Dutch and German speakers can choose the article early; Italian speakers must wait for the next word's sounds.
:::

::: footer
Miozzo & Caramazza 1999, as discussed in Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 170 to 171
:::

## Two hypotheses

- **Gender selection interference (GSIH):** the distractor's **gender feature** competes with the target's gender feature (Schriefers 1993).
- **Determiner selection interference (DSIH):** the distractor's **article** competes with the target's article (Miozzo & Caramazza 1999).

::: {.prompt}
Both predict a singular effect. What would tell them apart?
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 170 to 172
:::

## Predictions: the plural

| Response | Incongruent distractor | Gender differs? | Article differs? |
|---|---|---|---|
| *der Stuhl* (one chair) | *Kleid* | yes | yes: *der* vs. *das* |
| *die Stühle* (two chairs) | *Kleid* | yes | no: *die* for every gender |

- **GSIH:** effect in the singular **and** the plural.
- **DSIH:** effect in the **singular only**.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, p. 172
:::

## Eight experiments {.smaller}

| Exp. | Language | Response | What varies |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | German | Det + N | one or two objects |
| 1b | German | Adj + N | one or two objects |
| 1c | German | Det + Adj + N | one or two objects |
| 2a | Dutch | Det + N | one or two objects; three SOAs |
| 2b | Dutch | Det + N | number cued by a tone |
| 3 | Dutch | Det + N | singular and plural distractors |
| 4a | Dutch | Adj + N | singular only; extra related distractors |
| 4b | Dutch | Det + Adj + N | same pictures as 4a |

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003; 15 to 27 participants per experiment; 60 German pictures, 22 Dutch pictures
:::

## Experiment 1: conditions {.smaller}

|  | Congruent: *Keks* (der) | Incongruent: *Kleid* (das) | Response: 1a, 1b, 1c |
|---|---|---|---|
| One object | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🪑</span><span class="word">KEKS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🪑</span><span class="word">KLEID</span></span> | der Stuhl<br>roter Stuhl<br>der rote Stuhl |
| Two objects | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🪑🪑</span><span class="word">KEKS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🪑🪑</span><span class="word">KLEID</span></span> | die Stühle<br>rote Stühle<br>die roten Stühle |

Same 60 pictures in 1a, 1b, 1c. In 1b and 1c the pictures are red or green; the responses above are for red.

::: footer
Items from Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Appendix A; procedure pp. 174 to 175
:::

## Experiment 1: results {.smaller}

| Exp. | Response | Singular effect | Plural effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a | Det + N | **+20 ms** | −9 ms |
| 1b | Adj + N | −3 ms | −6 ms |
| 1c | Det + Adj + N | **+16 ms** | −7 ms |

Effect = incongruent minus congruent. **Bold** = reliable by participants and by items.

- Articles in the singular: effect. One article in the plural: no effect.
- Adjective suffix only (1b): no effect in either number.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Tables 1 to 3, pp. 176 to 177
:::

## Why Experiment 2?

- **Language:** the effect was first found in Dutch (Schriefers 1993). Does the plural null hold there too?
- **Timing:** the effect was largest at SOA 0 in Schriefers (1993). Experiment 1 tested only SOA 0, so 2a adds a distractor 100 ms before and 100 ms after the picture.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, p. 179
:::

## Experiment 2a: conditions {.smaller}

|  | Congruent: *glas* (het) | Incongruent: *klap* (de) | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| One object | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | het boek |
| Two objects | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | de boeken |

Every cell at three SOAs: distractor 100 ms before, with, or 100 ms after the picture.

::: footer
Items from Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Appendix B; procedure pp. 179 to 181
:::

## Experiment 2a: results

| Distractor onset | Singular effect | Plural effect |
|---|---|---|
| 100 ms before the picture | **+16 ms** | +2 ms |
| with the picture | **+31 ms** | +11 ms |
| 100 ms after the picture | **+36 ms** | +6 ms |

Singular effect at every SOA; no reliable plural effect at any SOA.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Table 6, p. 181
:::

## Experiment 2b: conditions {.smaller}

**Concern:** on seeing two objects, speakers could pick *de* at once without checking gender.

|  | Congruent: *glas* (het) | Incongruent: *klap* (de) | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low tone | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | het boek |
| High tone | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | de boeken |

Always one object. The tone comes 300 ms after picture onset.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, p. 180
:::

## Experiment 2b: results

| Singular effect | Plural effect |
|---|---|
| **+20 ms** | −2 ms |

::: {.claim}
The plural null holds even when the article cannot be chosen from the picture alone.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Table 7, pp. 181 to 182
:::

## Experiment 3: conditions {.smaller}

- So far distractors were singular, so a neuter distractor could activate *het*.
- Plural distractors were added: their article is *de* for every gender.

|  | Congruent, sg | Congruent, pl | Incongruent, sg | Incongruent, pl |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| *het boek* | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">GLAZEN</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖</span><span class="word">KLAPPEN</span></span> |
| *de boeken* | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">GLAS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">GLAZEN</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">KLAP</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">📖📖</span><span class="word">KLAPPEN</span></span> |

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 183 to 184; plural forms of the Appendix B distractors
:::

## Experiment 3: results

| Target | Singular distractor | Plural distractor |
|---|---|---|
| Singular | **+21 ms** | **+22 ms** |
| Plural | 0 ms | −4 ms |

::: {.claim}
Only the distractor's gender matters. Number comes from the picture.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Table 10, pp. 183 to 185
:::

## Experiment 4: conditions {.smaller}

| Congruent | Incongruent | Semantic | Phonological |
|---|---|---|---|
| <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🐑</span><span class="word">NEST</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🐑</span><span class="word">KERS</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🐑</span><span class="word">HERT</span></span> | <span class="stim mini"><span class="pic">🐑</span><span class="word">SCHAAK</span></span> |
| *nest* 'nest' (het) | *kers* 'cherry' (de) | *hert* 'deer' (het) | *schaak* 'chess' (het) |

Response to a red sheep: *rood schaap* (4a), *het rode schaap* (4b).

One object only; pictures red, green, blue, or purple.

::: footer
Items from Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Appendix C; procedure pp. 185 to 186
:::

## Experiment 4: results {.smaller}

| Exp. | Response | Congruent | Incongruent | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4a | Adj + N | 738 ms | 734 ms | −4 ms |
| 4b | Det + Adj + N | 750 ms | 766 ms | **+16 ms** |

- Phonologically related distractors sped naming in both: the distractors were processed.
- 4a fails to replicate Schriefers (1993, Exp. 2).
- 4b: reliable by participants, marginal by items (*p* = .056).

::: {.claim}
With the same materials, the effect appears only when the response contains an article.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, Tables 11 and 12, pp. 185 to 187
:::

# What the results mean

## What the eight experiments show

| Response | Article differs by gender? | Congruency effect? | Experiments |
|---|---|---|---|
| Singular + article | [yes]{.hl} | [yes]{.hl} | 1a, 1c, 2a, 2b, 3, 4b |
| Plural + article | no | no | 1a, 1c, 2a, 2b, 3 |
| Adjective + noun | no article | no | 1b, 4a |

::: {.claim}
The "gender congruency effect" is a **determiner congruency effect**.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 187 to 190
:::

## Where is the competition?

| Level | Competitive? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Gender feature | no | gender still differs in the plural, but no effect |
| Article form | [yes]{.hl} | effect only where the articles differ |

::: {.claim}
Selecting a noun makes its gender available automatically; only forms compete.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 187 to 188
:::

## Why no effect with adjective suffixes?

| Option | Idea |
|---|---|
| Free vs. bound | free-standing *der* competes; the suffix *-er* in *rot-er* does not |
| Timing | suffixes attach late, after the competition is resolved |

The paper cannot choose between them.

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 187 to 188
:::

## Article competition and serial models

|  | Word | Gender | Article |
|---|---|---|---|
| Picture, said | *Stuhl* | masculine | *der* |
| Distractor, never said | *Kleid* | neuter | [*das*]{.hl} |

::: {.claim}
*das* is not on the screen, so only *Kleid*'s gender can activate it. Discrete serial models (Levelt et al. 1999) do not allow this; cascading models do.
:::

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, pp. 173 and 188; Levelt, Roelofs & Meyer 1999
:::

## Is gender skipped in the plural?

If it were, gender competition (GSIH) could survive the plural null. Naming without distractors:

|  | Masculine | Feminine | Neuter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Singular | [*der*]{.hl} 653 ms | *die* 655 ms | [*das*]{.hl} 647 ms |
| Plural | *die* 673 ms | *die* 649 ms | *die* 681 ms |
| Plural cost | [+20 ms]{.hl} | −6 ms | [+34 ms]{.hl} |

::: {.claim}
The singular article competes with *die*: gender is still active in the plural.
:::

::: footer
Schriefers, Jescheniak & Hantsch 2002, Exp. 1, Table 1; cited in Schiller & Caramazza 2003, p. 189
:::

## Agreement needs plural gender

| Phrase | Pronoun | Gender from |
|---|---|---|
| *[eine]{.hl} der [Katzen]{.hl} miaute* | feminine | *Katzen*, plural |
| *[einer]{.hl} der [Hunde]{.hl} bellte* | masculine | *Hunde*, plural |

'one of the cats meowed', 'one of the dogs barked'

::: footer
Schiller & Caramazza 2003, p. 189
:::

## A Distributed Morphology reading

**Not in the paper.**

| Vocabulary Item | Inserted in |
|---|---|
| D[definite, neuter, singular] ↔ /het/ | het boek |
| D[definite] ↔ /de/ | de tafel, de tafels, de boeken |

::: {.claim}
**Impoverishment:** delete [gender] on plural D. The noun keeps its gender, so gender competition on D is possible only in the singular.
:::

::: footer
Halle & Marantz 1993; Harley & Noyer 1999; week 5 DM decks
:::

## Testing the Impoverishment reading

| Finding | Impoverishment | Article competition (DSIH) |
|---|---|---|
| Singular effect only | yes | yes |
| Plural cost: +20, −6, +34 ms | [no]{.hl} | yes |
| No adjective effect | [only if suffixes are late]{.hl} | yes |

::: footer
Not in Schiller & Caramazza 2003
:::
